newsitem.title: UK: HSBC shares down as SBC Warburg downgrades.
newsitem.headline: HSBC shares down as SBC Warburg downgrades.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc fell on Monday as the stock went ex-dividend and analysts at SBC Warburg downgraded their recommendation to "hold" from "add", dealers said.
The shares were 42-1/2p weaker at 21.25 stg by 0937 GMT.
Analysts at SBC Warburg were not immediately available for comment but market sources said the investment bank had downgraded HSBC.
"There's been a downgrade and that's knocked the shares, along with general market weakness," one dealer said. "But they're not looking too bad considering they've gone ex-dividend."
Barclays Plc and Standard Chartered Plc also went ex-dividend. Barclays shares were down 10-1/2p at 13.86 stg and Standard Chartered fell 14p to 1003-1/2.

Elsewhere in the sector, Lloyds TSB Group Plc was three pence weaker at 722 and Abbey National Plc was down four at 794. Alliance & Leicester Plc lost four pence to 616-1/2 and Halifax Plc fell four to 719.
"The sector is performing reasonably well as a whole. It's slightly outperforming the overall index, although there's not a lot in it," one market-maker said.
